kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Borrowed, originally in the form سُنَّار (sunnār) of which سِنَّوْر (sinnawr) may be an old diminutive, from Aramaic שׁוּנָּרָא / ܫܘܢܪܐ (šunnāra), ܣܢܘܪܐ (sannūrā), most likely from Akkadian 𒊓𒀀 (šurānum), whence also Hebrew שֻׁנָּר (šunnār). It is not clear whether the term is ultimately Semitic or not. John Huehnergard considers the possibility that the Akkadian term derives from a root *sur- which might be connected to هِرّ (hirr), since a change of Proto-Semitic *s to West Semitic *h is known to have occurred in a very small number of words.
